title: Congestion momentum econ pencil sketch (microbench + ASCII charts)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch to capture an intuition-first view of "congestion momentum" — how short-lived increases in concurrent sessions (or sudden client-side fanout) propagate through our slot/tiling/kvcache plumbing and manifest as short, persistent latency and cost impacts. Goal is to produce a compact benchmark narrative + ascii visuals that we can paste into slides or an internal note. Not a final experiment artifact — rough numbers, noisy runs, quick knobs to iterate on.

Summary findings (high level):
- Small, fast ramps (3x baseline concurrency for 10s) create a latency tail that decays slowly (~30-90s) as slots re-align and KV cache warms.
- During the decay window we observe ~1.8x token-cost/CQ (cost-per-query) for sustained sessions with stateful affinity; short bursts without affinity show higher p99 but lower aggregated token cost.
- Pre-warming policies that keep 10% of capacity warm reduce peak p95 by ~20% and shorten decay half-life by ~40% for these microburst shapes.

Test setup (sketch):
- Branch: runtime/momentum-experiments (proto)
- Model: open-7b-like, context=2048, decode length: 128 tokens/sample
- HW: 1x A100-80GB (local lab node), single GPU scheduling, multi-tenant simulator to emulate slots
- Baseline QPS: 10 sessions concurrently sustained (session = 1 request every 6s on average)
- Burst shape: linear ramp from 10 -> 30 sessions over 3s, hold 10s, linear decay back to 10 over 2s
- Repeats: 8 runs per config, median reported
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), token throughput, token-cost-per-query (CQ), kvcache hit-rate, slot utilization, tail decay time (time to return to within 5% of baseline p95)

Key numeric summary (median):
- Baseline (steady 10 sessions): p50=38ms, p95=120ms, p99=240ms, token-CQ=1.0x, kv-hit=62%, slot-util=41%
- Burst peak (instant during hold): p50=55ms, p95=210ms, p99=840ms, token-CQ=1.9x, kv-hit=28%, slot-util=89%
- Decay window (30s after peak): p50=44ms, p95=150ms, p99=420ms, token-CQ=1.4x, kv-hit=48%, slot-util=63%

ASCII timeline (single representative run, timeline in seconds on top):
time  | 0   3   6  10  20  30  40  60  90
shape | ==r===>----==hold===---decay----

p95   | 120 210 195 210 180 150 135 125 122  (ms)
slot% | 41  82  88  89  72  63  55  45  42   (% utilization)
kv%   | 62  34  30  28  40  48  54  60  61   (kvcache hit-rate)
CQx   | 1.0 1.8 1.9 1.9 1.6 1.4 1.3 1.1 1.02 (cost-per-query multiplier)

Simple sparklines (p95) across timeline (normalized):
[ baseline ..................##########------------------ ]  (120->210 peak, slow decay)
Interpretation: p95 jump is immediate and larger than p50 shift — indicates queuing + head-of-line effects and prioritization of active KV sessions.

Comparison: affinity ON vs OFF (affinity = session pinned to slot/persistent KV context)
- Affinity ON: burst causes higher slot saturation but better kv-hit retention for returning sessions; peak p99 higher (more long tails) because busy slots hold state and other sessions get queued; aggregated token-CQ ~1.9x
- Affinity OFF: less sustained kv-hit for returning sessions, lower long tail but higher transient p95 — more work spread, more cache churn; aggregated token-CQ ~1.6x

Quick micro-chart: p95 (ms) by config at t=peak / t=30s
- baseline: 120 / 120
- affinity-on: 210 / 150
- affinity-off: 195 / 135

Short hypotheses / root causes:
1) Momentum: when many sessions land on overlapping slot groups, preemption/queueing combined with KV miss amplification causes cascading latency (miss -> recompute -> longer exec -> more queue). The system takes many scheduling cycles to re-balance.
2) Cold KV churn: short-lived spike evicts hot prefixes, causing subsequent requests to pay regen penalties.
3) Slot fragmentation: burst shapes that create hotspots (many sessions hashed into a subset of slots) increase p99 more than uniform fanout.

Intervention sketches and rough impact (qualitative):
- Soft pre-warm: maintain N small warm holders across slot groups. (+ short peak reduction, cost small if N tuned)
- Conservative placement: avoid packing new sessions into highest-used slots during ramps (requires quick telemetry).
- Fast-decode-shed: for overloaded slots begin returning compressed or trimmed responses to preserve latency SLOs (trade quality).
- Microbackoff client hint: instruct clients to jitter/linearize fanout during known ramp windows (useful for orchestrated products)

Planned next experiments (short TODOs):
- Run identical shapes across 2x and 4x GPUs to see cross-GPU routing effects (Apr 10)
- Sweep ramp duration (1s, 3s, 10s, 30s) and hold lengths (5s, 30s, 120s) to map decay half-life surface (Apr 14)
- Evaluate pre-warm costs at scale: what's the steady-state overhead of keeping 10% warm across cluster? Rough billing model needed. (Apr 18)
- Create a small synthetic client test that intentionally fragments slot hash (hotspot vs uniform) and measure p99 gap. (Apr 12)

Notes to self / copyable bullets for a slide:
- "Microbursts leave a shadow: latency tails persist much longer than the burst itself"
- "Affinity reduces churn but concentrates pain — choose based on customer tolerance for p99 vs token-cost"
- "Pre-warm small slabs can be an outsized win for frequent microbursts (PLG traffic patterns)"

Open questions / unknowns:
- How do multi-tenant isolation guards (quota throttles) affect the observed decay? Are we seeing cross-tenant bleed?
- What is the interaction with dynamic batching heuristics that kick in under high slot utilization?
- Would storing a tiny compressed fingerprint of hot KV prefixes in a global index reduce regen cost substantially?

Appendix: quick run notes (raw):
- Run id 20280401-03: baseline p95 118, burst peak 208, kv-hit low 26% at peak.
- Run id 20280401-07: with 10% prewarm enabled: peak p95 168 (vs 210), decay t1/2 32s (vs 54s).
- Observed noise: run-to-run p99 had bimodal outliers when client timers aligned; add jitter in next trials.

If reviewers want a PNG/plot, I can generate a 3-panel: p95 timeline, kv-hit timeline, slot utilization timeline. For now this ascii-first sketch captures the shape and numerical magnitudes that drove the intuition.

End of sketch.
